• Armor Class is the fourth miss roll and the build mostly ignores it. The Mark is what AC-based defence this build has, and it is on the enemy: -10 AC on the Marked target is for the party’s benefit, not yours.

    • Layer 3: the hit does less. Physical Resistance Rating reduces physical damage by 100/(100+PRR) (PRR page): 20 PRR takes a sixth off, 50 takes a third, 100 takes half. Each point is about +1% effective hit points. Light armor gives PRR equal to your Base Attack Bonus with proficiency, which Ranger has; the rest is items. Magical Resistance Rating does the same for fire, cold, electric, acid, sonic, force, light, negative and the rest (MRR page), capped at 100 in light armor. Survivalist adds +3 PRR; the Divine epic past lives add up to +36; the Reaper tree’s Grim Barricade adds more. The fully filled level-36 kit contributes unverified gear PRR (modeled raw 133); the whole-character defense totals remain unverified. At level 10 you have perhaps 20 PRR, which cuts physical damage by a sixth. That gap is why levelling hurts.

    Layer 4: the hit is not a critical or a sneak attack. Fortification is a percentage chance to turn a critical hit or sneak attack against you into a normal hit (Fortification page); “most players strive for roughly +10% fortification per level”. Dauntless Marking does nothing for you here: it is the enemy’s fortification the Mark cuts. Your own comes from items. Combined Fortification remains unverified for the selected kit; see the current source audit. While levelling, the Lotus Mail (59%) plus the Nocturne Ring (Insightful 29%) at 5-9 is the first real fortification; before that you have none, and every critical hit lands.

    Layer 5: the save. Three saves (Saving throw page), and this build is uneven across them.

    • Reflex is the strong one: Ranger and Rogue both have good Reflex progressions (Ranger +6 at level 9; class table), Insightful Reflexes puts your Intelligence modifier on it instead of Dexterity, and Evasion from Ranger 9 (or Rogue 2) turns a passed save into no damage at all. Shadowdancer’s The Darkest Luck core upgrades it to Improved Evasion at 35 in the destiny order (a failed save is half damage). Walker’s Guidance gives both for 12 seconds on demand. Traps, breath weapons, fireballs, lightning bolts: this is where the build is safe, as long as it is in light armor and not helpless.

reviewed_replacements.label: chains-type-reviewed-6
reviewed_replacements.before:
Monster saves rise by about +1.5 per skull, concealment bypass by 5% per skull (capped at 30%), and crowd control is shortened but never below 6 seconds. Reapers of the Vengeance and Despair types appear from five skulls, the Doom Reaper from seven.

While levelling (levels 1-19)

The fully filled level-36 kit contributes unverified gear PRR (modeled raw 133). Combined Fortification remains unverified; combined Dodge, threat reduction and whole-character defenses also need their source checks. The current audit separates supported gear contributions from those unresolved totals. While levelling, the character has light-armor PRR equal to its Base Attack Bonus, whatever the levelling set adds, a few percent of dodge, Evasion from Ranger 9, and no threat reduction at all. It is, for nineteen levels, a d10-hit-die archer with no self-healing and the group’s highest damage. That is why it dies.

Where the levelling set is thin. The set was lifted slot for slot from a repeater dataset and carries that build’s priorities, and the gaps are visible in its own lines (Gear section): at 1-4 the armor’s PRR 7 and the bracer’s Sheltering 7 are the same bonus type, so the total is 7, and there is no fortification at all; at 5-9 the only Constitution item is dropped for Seeker boots and the cloak upgrades at 7 and 9 both lose False Life; at 15-19 one bracer slot is spent on healing spell power the build cannot use; at 20-29 the necklace and bracers carry Strength, Shatter, Wisdom and Wizardry, nothing for a bow, while fortification sits at 94% and False Life is gone. A reworked levelling set with a survivability floor in every band (fortification, the best physical sheltering available, Constitution, False Life, a Will-save or Spell Saves item, and Ghost Touch ammunition for Reaper) is the planned rework of the Gear section; until it lands, treat the set as the offence and fill the dead slots yourself from the wiki’s item lists, starting with the skill diamonds under Skills.

What to do now, in order of effect.

Abilities or skills that stack add their effects together. For example, modifiers of +1 Save all and +2 Save against fear stack to create a total +3 to Save versus fear (in addition to the +1 to Save against everything else). In most cases however, only the strongest effect applies. For example, having non-stacking +3 and +5 modifiers is only worth a +5 bonus, not +8.

Magical Resistance Rating (abbreviated MRR) is a form of damage mitigation that was introduced with Update 23. It provides a percentage reduction in damage from acid, sonic, fire, electric, cold, alignment, light, positive, negative, poison, rust, and force (since Update 78). MRR is granted through multiple sources (items, feats, enhancements) and stacks with itself. Multiple effects granting an Enhancement bonus to Magical Resistance do not stack.
Character sheets show the Magical Resistance Rating of the player next to the elemental resistances. MRR is applied after Elemental Resistance. MRR is applied to the damage that passes through the resistance and this is always rounded down. As such if a player would take 20 damage before resists or MRR was applied and had 10 resistance and 60 MRR (37.5% reduction), the result is:
(20 - 10) * (100 - 37.5)% = 6.25 round down to 6
14 damage will be resisted.

Magical Resistance Rating (MRR) should work vs. traps and most other damage sources (not just spells). If you are wielding a heavy or tower shield, your MRR values are considered doubled against damage that can be halved with a Reflex save (whether traps or spells). See Physical Resistance Rating#Monsters with PRR for information about reducing MRR of your enemies and how that affects the damage of your magical attacks. All of the properties listed are able to go into the negatives. Going from 0 to -10 PRR provides the same difference in damage against the target as going from 10 PRR to 0 PRR. The same is true of MRR and Melee Power/Ranged Power. So! Even though a large portion of monsters do not innately have positive values of those stats, effects that debuff still help to defeat them.
